subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test for FinWise
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwise.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@finwise.com>
Date: 2027-03-08T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test for FinWise

Hi Alex & Priya,

Thanks for taking the time today — helpful to understand FinWise's usage patterns and goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Summary of SLOs you mentioned:
- Latency: target p95 across interactive endpoints <= 200ms (desktop web) and p95 <= 300ms for mobile SDK calls.
- Throughput: peak sustained 1,200 requests/minute, burst to 2,500 reqs/min for 10–15 minute windows.
- Concurrency: expect up to ~120 concurrent sessions during peak.
- Streaming: primary flows use streaming tokens for assistant responses (we should validate chunk sizes); streaming latency target ~100ms per chunk.

Customer-led load test ask: you mentioned running a k6 load plan next week. For us to support a smooth test we need:
- Confirmation of a 2-hour test window (we proposed Tue 2027-03-09 17:00–19:00 PT).
- IP allowlist: please share the public IPs/CIDR from FinWise test runners (we'll open firewall on our side).
- Test accounts: we'll provision a test API key and a sandbox org with the same routing/pinning as prod.
- k6/Locust script: if you already have a script, please share; otherwise our SRE team can provide a starter k6 script and dataset.

Action items / next steps:
1) Alex/Priya — confirm the 17:00–19:00 PT window or propose alternate. Share test runner IPs if available.
2) Redwood (Marissa/Aditya/Rishi) — we'll prepare a k6 starter script, create a test account, and provide an allowlist IPs sheet + credentials.
3) Both teams — decide whether the test will hit streaming endpoints or non-streaming (we need this to configure the script).

Attachments: I will follow up with the k6 starter script and an SLO spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Logan
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwise.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@finwise.com>
Date: 2027-03-08T17:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test for FinWise

Thanks Logan — that summary matches our internal notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- Window: Tue 2027-03-09 17:00–19:00 PT works for our infra team.
- IPs: our test fleet will come from 198.51.100.0/24 (primary) and 203.0.113.45 (jumpbox). Please allowlist those.
- Streaming: we want to exercise both streaming and non-streaming flows. The main user journey (assistant) is streaming; we can run a blended plan with ~70% streaming traffic.
- Data: we'll use anonymized production-like payloads (already sanitized).

Can you provide the API key and test org by EOD tomorrow (Mon 2027-03-08)? Also if you can share a basic k6 script, that would speed us up — we may tune it on our side.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Engineering, FinWise
alex.johnson@finwise.com
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-08T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test for FinWise

Marissa / Aditya — forwarding FinWise confirmation. High-level requirements:
- Peak: 1,200 reqs/min sustained, bursts to 2,500 reqs/min for ~10–15m.
- Concurrency: ~120 concurrent sessions.
- Traffic mix: blended with 70% streaming, 30% non-streaming.
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 200ms (desktop), p95 <= 300ms (mobile), streaming chunk latency ~100ms.

Please prepare the following before EOD Mon (2027-03-08):
1) Starter k6 script (file name finwise-loadtest-k6-script.js) that supports streaming simulation (use event streaming where possible) and a non-streaming path. Make payloads configurable so FinWise can tune payload size and arrival rates.
2) Test account & API key (limited scope, rate-limited, logs enabled) and a creds file for exchange (redwood-test-account-creds.txt).
3) Allowlist request for infra: open inbound from 198.51.100.0/24 and 203.0.113.45 on the test env. Add this to the resourcing doc.
4) Quick SLO spreadsheet showing target vs current baseline (slo-targets.xlsx).

Aditya — can you confirm whether streaming endpoints require different ingress routing or any special kernel settings for our runtime to ensure accurate measurement of per-chunk latency? Rishi / Marissa — please include any notes for the customer about cold-cache vs warmed-cache expectations during the test.

Thanks — we want to have creds + script to Alex by EOD Monday so they can validate before the Tue window.

Logan
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test for FinWise

On Mon, Mar 8, 2027 at 5:45 PM Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marissa / Aditya — forwarding FinWise confirmation. High-level requirements:
> - Peak: 1,200 reqs/min sustained, bursts to 2,500 reqs/min for ~10–15m.
> - Concurrency: ~120 concurrent sessions.
> - Traffic mix: blended with 70% streaming, 30% non-streaming.

We can meet these numbers on the dedicated test cluster but a few notes:
- Streaming endpoints are served by the streaming runtime path; we need to ensure clients use chunked transfer (server-sent events). For accurate per-chunk latency we must not enable aggressive server-side bundling. I will set the runtime to "per-chunk" mode for the test env.
- I will provision the test org and API key today and add strict rate/usage caps (so they can't hit prod accidentally).
- Attached is a starter k6 script (finwise-loadtest-k6-script.js) and a small readme in the repo. The script includes toggles for "streaming" vs "non-streaming" flows and configurable RPS.

I'll also request the infra team to open inbound from FinWise IPs (198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.45) to the test cluster.

I'll upload the creds and SLO workbook to the shared drive and DM the link.

- Aditya

Attachment: finwise-loadtest-k6-script.js (k6 script)
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwise.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@finwise.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-10T10:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test for FinWise

Alex — quick confirmation and handoff: 

- Test window: Tue 2027-03-09 17:00–19:00 PT (confirmed).
- IPs allowlisted: 198.51.100.0/24 and 203.0.113.45.
- Test creds: attached redwood-test-account-creds.txt (API key + org id, limited scope).
- Scripts: attached finwise-loadtest-k6-script.js (starter k6) and a Drive link with SLO targets: https://drive.google.com/finwise-loadplan.

Notes for the run:
- Aditya set the runtime to per-chunk streaming mode. Expect warmed-cache results will be ~10–15% better than cold-cache; we recommend running one 20-minute warmup before the official window.
- We'll capture detailed token-level latency and per-request tracing; please share any additional traces you want correlated.

Please confirm you received the creds and that the FinWise infra team can start the run. We'll have on-call infra (Rishi) and SRE (Marissa) monitoring during the window.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to results.

Logan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
